setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.
steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.
steps.title: Save D as the root

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.
steps.title: Hear that nothing changed

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.
steps.title: Apply slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.
steps.title: Hear D major

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor switches to slot 3, which lights dimly, and slot 2 stays bright.
steps.title: Select slot 3 for editing

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop: the phrase keeps playing in D major (62, 64, 66, 67), because selecting a slot for editing never changes what you hear. Now hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). Slot 2 is both the applied scale and the one being edited.
steps.title: Select the applied scale for editing

steps.caption: Turn E3 two detents up so the root moves from D to E and press K3. Tap Play, then Stop. Saving a scale that playback is using changes it at once: the phrase now plays E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69.
steps.title: Saving an applied scale changes the sound

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor moves to slot 3 and slot 2 is still the applied scale.
steps.title: Select slot 3 again

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 again. A long press on the slot already selected for editing turns the global scale off: no slot button is lit and the editing selection clears. A short press on the applied slot also turns global scale off, but keeps that slot selected for editing. These gestures differ in their editing selection.
steps.title: Turn the global scale off

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. With no scale, pattern notes play as semitone steps from the root: C, C#, D, D# (MIDI 60, 61, 62, 63).
steps.title: Hear chromatic notes

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). The scale returns with the edits you saved. Tap Play, then Stop: E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69. Recap: a tap applies a slot; K1 plus a tap, or a one-second hold, selects a slot for editing without applying it; a second hold on the slot being edited turns the global scale off; saving with K3 changes the sound only if that slot is the applied one.
steps.title: Apply a scale again
